name: Stratus Shard
geological_features: Deep strip-mining trenches carved by automated excavation systems
Exposed mineral strata in canyon walls revealing geological history
Impact craters repurposed as equipment staging areas
specific_features: A network of autonomous mining drones operating on century-old directives
Orbital tether anchor points from a decommissioned space elevator
Vast tailings fields of processed regolith sorted by mineral content
resources: Refined ingot stockpiles left by previous mining operations
description: Stratus Shard is a cold, airless rock scarred beyond recognition by centuries of automated mining. Its surface is a grid of geometric trenches and terraced pits, the original terrain so thoroughly excavated that the planet's silhouette has visibly changed since its first survey. A thin wisp of atmosphere clings to the deepest canyons, just enough to carry the faint whine of machinery that has never been told to stop.

There is no weather on Stratus Shard, only the slow crawl of shadow as the planet rotates and the occasional sparkle of micrometeorite impacts on exposed mineral faces. The silence is mechanical rather than natural, broken at precise intervals by the rumble of autonomous haulers depositing loads at processing centers that still sort and refine ore for pickup ships that stopped coming decades ago. Stockpiles of refined metal grow taller each year, glinting in the starlight like monuments to forgotten commerce.

The mining claim on Stratus Shard was originally held by Veydric Industrial, a corporation that dissolved during a sector-wide financial collapse. With no entity to issue a shutdown command, the automated systems defaulted to their extraction protocols and have continued working with tireless efficiency. Legal scholars debate who owns the accumulated wealth, while salvage operators note that the drones' defensive subroutines remain fully operational and do not distinguish between pirates and legitimate claimants.

For those willing to navigate the legal ambiguity and dodge the territorial mining drones, Stratus Shard represents a fortune in pre-processed materials. The stockpiles alone could supply a shipyard for years. But the planet also serves as a cautionary object lesson in autonomous systems, and more than one academic expedition has come here simply to study what happens when machines outlive their masters.
